paragraphs.text: Lesson 26, Arguing and Swearing
Yesterday you learned how to disagree politely, but what if the disagreement turns into a real
argument?
Listen to this conversation between Christine and Tara, who share an apartment, to learn
some of the common phrases used for arguing.
Conversation number one, Arguing
Hey Tara, when are you going to clean up the bathroom?
I've asked you to do it a zillion times.
Maybe when you quit bugging me about it.
What's your problem?
Other people use that bathroom too, you know, and your makeup and stuff is all over the place.
Well, excuse me for not being perfectly organized like you.
Don't talk to me like that.
It's a simple request, just clean up the damn bathroom.
Do it yourself.
What did you just say to me?
I said, if it's so important for the bathroom to be clean, why don't you do it yourself?
You're always on my case about something and you never shut up.
Yeah, well, that's because you never help out.
The kitchen's a mess too.
Oh sure, blame it all on me.
You use the kitchen way more than I do.
You know what?
I'm not going to waste my breath arguing with you.
When I get back from yoga class, the kitchen and bathroom had better be clean, or else.
Whatever.
Whatever.
Conversation vocabulary and phrases.
Christine starts by reminding Tara to clean the bathroom and saying, I've asked you to
do it a zillion times.
This is a way to express frustration and call attention to the fact that despite many requests,
Tara has not done what was asked.
Zillion is not a real number.
It just means a huge number.
We have two similar phrases.
I've asked you to do it a zillion times.
And, I've told you a zillion times.
For example, I've told you a zillion times not to throw your dirty clothes on the floor.
Tara then replies that maybe she'll clean the bathroom when Christine stops bugging her
about it.
The word bugging, or nagging, means to remind somebody in an annoying way.
Here are some phrases.
Quit bugging me.
Quit nagging me.
Quit bothering me.
Bothering means annoying in general, not necessarily reminding about something.
The dialogue has two argumentative phrases that begin with what?
What's your problem?
What did you just say to me?
We use that phrase when you can't believe the rude thing the other person said.
Tara says, excuse me, in a very sarcastic way.
Sometimes the attitude you have and the way you pronounce a word or phrase makes a difference
in its meaning or function.
Compare these situations.
Excuse me.
Do you know what time it is?
Excuse me for not being perfectly organized like you.
Hi.
How are you?
Fine.
You're a liar.
You can forget about our agreement.
The deal's off.
Fine.
I wouldn't want to do business with an idiot like you anyway.
Would you like a cup of tea?
Yes, please.
Why are you signing up for a marathon?
You couldn't run a mile if your life depended on it.
Oh, please.
I'm in way better shape than you.
Could you please clean up the kitchen?
Oh, sure.
The kitchen's a mess, too.
Oh, sure.
Blame it all on me.
You can see that if you pronounce the phrases with a pleasant tone, then it sounds nice.
But, if you pronounce the expressions with a sarcastic tone, then it expresses frustration
and contributes to the argument.
Later in the dialogue, Tara says, you never shut up.
The expression, shut up, is a rather rude way to tell someone to be quiet.
Finally, Christine says that the kitchen and bathroom must be cleaned by the time she comes
home or else.
Ending a sentence like this with or else expresses a threat which is not directly spoken or defined.
It means there will be some negative consequence if the other person doesn't do what you say.
For example, a mother might say to her son, finish your homework now or else.
That means if he doesn't finish his homework, there will be some negative consequence.
The mother will take away his video games or not let him go to a party or make him do extra
chores.
The threat is not directly stated, but it will be something bad.
Tara responds by saying, whatever.
This is a rude way to say you don't care about what the other person is saying and you aren't
interested in listening.
Now you know how to argue in English, but if the argument gets really bad, then you might
want some of the stronger words in the next section of this lesson.
Swearing in English.
In this section I'm going to explain some of the most common swears, bad words, in English
and how they are used.
Even if you don't want to use swear words yourself, it's still useful to recognize them
and understand them when you watch movies or hear other people talk.
Most of these swear words have less offensive versions which are used to substitute the word
if you don't want to speak quite as strongly or if you don't want to offend anyone.
Damn.
Damn it.
And God damn it.
Can all be used as exclamations of anger, frustration or annoyance.
The word damn can also be used as an adjective to give negative emphasis.
For example, I was late for work because my damn car wouldn't start.
We also have the phrase, I don't give a damn.
This means I don't care at all.
The less offensive version of damn is darn.
The word hell is also used as a swear word in English.
You can say, go to hell to insult the other person.
Another common use is asking, what the hell?
For example, what the hell happened?
What the hell is going on?
What the hell were you thinking?
Use hell in a question when you are asking the question angrily.
You can also use other question words like where or why.
Where the hell have you been?
Why the hell is it taking so long?
A less offensive version of hell is heck.
So you can say, what the heck happened?
And why the heck is it taking so long?
And this is much less offensive.
The word ass is a slang word for butt.
However, it's also used in insults.
He's an ass or he's an asshole.
These phrases are used to describe a stupid or mean person.
There are some other ways to use the word ass which are strong but not insulting.
Describing something as badass means it was cool and awesome.
Describing someone as a hard ass means a person who follows and enforces rules very strictly.
Piss and shit are slang words for urine and feces which can also be used in swearing.
Piss off is a rude way to say go away.
I'm pissed off.
Means I'm really angry.
A less offensive way to say this is I'm ticked off.
Bullshit means that's a lie.
It's a piece of shit or he's a piece of shit.
This means an object or a person is completely worthless.
We also have the adjective shitty meaning something is terrible or has bad quality.
For example, I have a shitty cell phone.
Shit can also be used in place of stuff or things.
For example, I'm moving this weekend so I have to pack up all my shit.
Remember, this is informal and a little bit offensive so you should only use it around
friends who you know very well.
There are also some positive ways to use the word shit.
If you say, he really knows his shit.
That means the person is very smart or knowledgeable.
If you say, that party was the shit, it means that the party was great.
Different from saying, that party was shit or that party was shitty, meaning the party
was terrible.
Remember, even in the cases where shit doesn't have a negative connotation, you should still
avoid talking like this in formal situations.
The word bitch can be used as an insult for a woman or girl.
If you say, she's such a bitch, that means the woman or girl is mean or annoying.
You can also use the adjective bitchy to describe someone's unpleasant personality or behavior.
Bitch can also be used as a verb to mean complain.
For example, there's nothing you can do about the situation so stop bitching about it.
We also have a phrasal verb to bitch someone out, meaning to yell at and criticize the person.
For example, my teacher bitched me out for coming to class late.
A less offensive version of this phrasal verb is chewed me out.
My teacher chewed me out for coming to class late.
Next, we have some sexual slang.
Both cunt and pussy are slang for vagina, and cock and dick are slang words for penis.
Calling a woman a cunt is extremely offensive.
Calling a man a pussy means he is weak and cowardly.
For example, you're such a pussy.
The less offensive way to say this is, you're such a chicken.
If you say, you're a dick, that is an insult for a man.
It means he is mean, selfish, inconsiderate, etc.
Finally, we have the word fuck, which is one of the most versatile swear words in the English language.
There are many different expressions, but here are some of the most common.
Fuck you, and go fuck yourself.
Are very offensive things to say to somebody at whom you are angry.
You can also say, fuck that, to express your anger at a situation.
The word fuck can be used as an adjective or an adverb to give a stronger and ruder emphasis to the sentence.
For example, I got fired from my fucking job.
That's fucking stupid.
I don't fucking care.
Fuck is also used in even stronger versions of the other expressions.
For example, we have what the heck, what the hell, and what the fuck, which is the strongest.
Oh shit is strong, and oh fuck is stronger.
Piss off is strong, and fuck off is stronger.
I don't give a damn, or I don't give a shit.
Are strong ways to express that you don't care, and I don't give a fuck is even stronger and ruder.
Finally, there are some phrasal verbs with the word fuck.
For example, to fuck someone over is to take advantage of someone in a horrible way.
Credit card companies fuck people over with their high interest rates.
Fuck around means to act silly, misbehave, and not do work.
For example, hey guys, stop fucking around and help me move this furniture.
A less offensive version is mess around, and also goof around.
Fuck up means to make a mistake.
The less offensive version of this is mess up.
For example, I fucked up.
I printed the wrong phone number on my business cards.
You've finished lesson 26.
Today's speaking task is to leave a message telling me about an argument you've had.
What were the reasons for the argument?
Who is it with, and how did you resolve it?
